reasons: Both answers wrongly make a large difference in certainty the main distinction, but A at least says «едва ли» is more formal and bookish and notes that «едва» on its own ('с трудом / только что') is a different word, while B leaves out register and the senses of «едва» completely. B's exercise is broken: a blank before «ли» would give «вряд ли ли», and it contains English ('hates cold'). B also wrongly bans «вряд ли не». A has its own flaws, such as the made-up mnemonic words «врядно» and «врядет» and a misused «едва ли не», but these are less harmful.

A: Presents «едва ли» as expressing much stronger certainty than «вряд ли»; the main difference is register (bookish vs neutral), not degree
Misuses «едва ли не» as if it meant 'definitely not'; it actually means 'almost, perhaps'
B: Gives numeric certainty ranges (70-80% vs 95-99%) and treats degree of certainty as the main difference; the actual difference is register
Claims «вряд ли не» + verb is ungrammatical, but constructions like «вряд ли он не знал» are normal
The exercise has a blank before «ли», so filling it in gives «вряд ли ли» / «едва ли ли»; it also contains English text
Leaves out that «едва ли» is bookish/formal and does not cover the «едва ли не» sense
